To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Endogenous glucocorticoids are involved in the regulation of the cardiovascular response to low sodium intake in rats, possibly by modulating the vascular reactivity to vasoconstrictors.
glucocorticoids are involved in the regulation of vascular tone in salt-restricted rat, possibly by increasing the vascular reactivity to noradrenaline and angiotensins.

(1) glucocorticoid administration restores mean blood pressure (MAP) nearly to basal level in rats with reduced sodium intake; (2) the antiglucocorti-coid RU 486 decreases MAP by approximately 14mmHg in rats with reduced salt intake; (3) glucocorticoids contribute to blood pressure regulation in rats with reduced Na intake by increasing vascular re-activity to vasoconstrictor agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the blood pressure and the renal functions, in the physiological conditions and in the pathological situations (hypertension, diabetes, etc...), and with the development of new drugs.
the study of the role of endogenous glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids in cardiovascular adaptation to sodium deprivation.
the role of glucocortioids in the control of blood pressure and sodium homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Gs play an important role in cardiovascular homeostasis, and that the mechanisms involved are not limited to the renin-angiotensin system, and include the modulation of the vascular reactivity to vasoconstrictor substances.
the antiglucocoticoid RU 486 has no effect on the cardiovascular system of the rat, but that it does have some effect on the blood pressure of sodium restricted rats.
Gs play an important role in the control of blood pressure in salt-restricted animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Gs are involved in the control of arterial pressure in sodium-depleted rats by increasing the sensitivity of the vascular system to vasoconstrictors.
the endogenous glucocorticoids play an important role in maintaining blood pressure in the sodium-restricted rats by increasing vascular reactivities to catecholamine and angiotensins.
glucocorticoid receptors are expressed in the vasculature and that glucocorticoids may play an important role in vascular reactivity to other pressor agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucocorticoids contribute to blood pressure regulation in sodium-depleted rats by enhancing vascular reactivity to vasoconstrictors.
glucocorticoids are a key regulator of the vascular response to low sodium.
